$comment: First-party plugin registry (AGL-417). THE single place that maps plugin ids to packages, register entry points, and API path prefixes. `tools/scripts/generate-plugin-manifests.mjs` turns this into the per-app generated loader manifests — the only files allowed to reference @aglyn/plugins-* outside libs/plugins. `catalog` is the plugin's row on the workspace and site switchboards (label, description, release flag, what switching it off for a site stops, and what a published site loses); the generator compiles every row, in `order`, into libs/aglyn plugin-manager/first-party-plugins.generated.ts, so a new plugin is declared here and nowhere in core (AGL-3080). An entry with no `catalog` is not on the switchboard. `capabilities` are further switchboard ids the same bundle serves. register keys: site = canvas/site components (client barrel), console = ConsoleExtension (client barrel), tenantApi/consoleApi = API handlers (/server entry), declarations = the light registrations core reads before any surface loads (`/declarations`, both apps, client and server), serverDeclarations = the same for the server alone (`/declarations.server`, platform-event subscriptions), consoleServerDeclarations = the same for the CONSOLE's server alone (`/declarations.console-server`, never loaded or bundled by the tenant runtime: for registrations that open what only the console holds), subprocessors = the third-party recipients the plugin's code sends data to, and its other hosts and its uses of hosts declared elsewhere (`/subprocessors`, called by the generator rather than at runtime, and written into the console's subprocessors manifest as data for the subprocessor inventory), planEntitlements = what each plan includes of the plugin's own entitlement keys (`/plan-entitlements`, called by the generator rather than at runtime and compiled into the catalog file as data that core's PLAN_ENTITLEMENTS composes, because the pricing tables and the plan comparison read it without loading a plugin), usageAxes = the meters the plugin contributes to the platform's cost model and utilization table, and the lines of spend it adds to a workspace's usage budget (`/usage-axes`, called by the generator and compiled into the catalog file as data, because the discount guardrail and the staff org page price a rollup without loading a plugin), videoEmbedProviders = the video hosts whose own player the plugin's Video element frames (`/video-embed-providers`, called by the generator and compiled into the catalog file as data, which the published page and the tenant's frame-src read without loading the plugin), tenantEmails = the emails a site sends its own customers through the plugin (`/tenant-emails`, called by the generator and compiled into the email lib's tenant email catalog as data, which the send path reads without loading the plugin). activityMutationPaths = the plugin's modules that create, transfer or destroy a durable customer object, which `tools/scripts/check-activity-coverage.mjs` holds to logging an activity entry like the platform's own. `alwaysOn` here is the LOADER's meaning — the bundle activates whatever ids `ensure()` is given, so it defeats the per-page narrowing in required-site-plugins.ts and belongs only to `mui`, which the canvas cannot render without. A plugin that merely may not be switched OFF says so with `alwaysOn` in FIRST_PARTY_PLUGINS instead. `modules` (AGL-3116) names the subpath a surface registers from when that surface's code must not ride with the package root's — each site surface has its own module, so a published page never loads a console registrar. `contributes` (AGL-3116, required) declares what the plugin adds and where, in the shape a marketplace manifest uses (core `plugin-contributions.ts`): `site.components` = the canvas component ids it registers, `site.features` = the site runtimes it mounts on every page of a site that switched it on, `console.slots` = the widget slots and panels it fills, `console.routes` / `console.orgRoutes` = the console routes it serves, `console.shell` = it draws a nav tab, a provider or a staff tab the shell renders on every screen. The loaders place a plugin by this declaration alone, so `apps/console/specs/plugin-contributions-declared.spec.ts` holds it to what the registrars actually register. `hostCollections` (AGL-3080) = the subcollections under a site the plugin owns (core `plugin-host-collections.ts`); a collection's `resource` is the KIND a client creates a document in it as, through the platform's generic create route — its field allow-list, plan counter, feature and stamps (core `plugin-host-resources.ts`), compiled and never registered, because that route is a security path. A collection's `siteExport` is how the whole-site backup carries it and what a restore writes back (core `plugin-site-export.ts`). `sitemapSections` (AGL-3080) = the child sitemaps the plugin's own pages fill (core `plugin-sitemap-sections.ts`), compiled because the tenant's sitemap is a published-site reader. `sitemapReaders` (AGL-3475) = child-sitemap families a plugin's READER lists, for pages no single site collection describes (core `plugin-sitemap-readers.ts`): each `section` is a family whose children are `{section}-{key}`, compiled so an index cannot silently drop them, with the reader registered from `serverDeclarations`. `consoleRedirects` (AGL-3080) = the plugin's old console addresses and where each answers now, in Next's redirect shape, compiled into `apps/console/constants/plugins.redirects.generated.json`, which the console's next.config.js spreads into its redirects. `siteBundleSections` (AGL-3080) = the sections of the whole-site backup the plugin answers for itself, data a host collection's `siteExport` cannot describe (core `plugin-site-bundle.ts`): declared here, registered from `serverDeclarations`, and an export fails rather than leaving a declared section out. `transferResources` (AGL-3523) = what the plugin can import and export, each a `TransferResourceDescriptor` from core `data-transfer/resource.ts` (key, label, scope, kinds, formats, limits; core `plugin-transfer-resources.ts`): declared here, the server half registered from `serverDeclarations` or `consoleServerDeclarations`, the client half from the console registrar loaded at the `transferResources` slot, and a job fails rather than leaving a declared resource out. `taxReturnSource: true` (AGL-3080) = the plugin sells through the platform's own account and registers a tax return source (core `plugin-tax-return-sources.ts`); the operator's sales tax return refuses to be filed while a declared source is unregistered. `revenueSource: true` (AGL-3080) = the plugin earns the operator a take through the platform's account and registers a revenue source (core `plugin-revenue-sources.ts`); the staff revenue report names a declared source it could not read rather than counting it as zero. `notificationCategories` (AGL-3080) = the preference buckets the plugin's notification types fall in, by the prefix before the dot: an `id` no other plugin and not the core owns, a `label` and `description` for the settings page, and `defaults` for the console and email channels; compiled into the catalog file and read by core `notifications.ts`, because the fan-out resolves channels in processes that load no plugin. The id keys stored preferences, so it is never renamed. `notificationDigests` (AGL-3080) = the digests the plugin sends on its own schedule: the `key` its on-by-default switch is stored under in `users/{uid}.digestPrefs`, and the switch's `label` and `description`, compiled the same way so the settings page draws it without loading the plugin. `interactionSteps` (AGL-3080) = the steps the plugin adds to interactions: the stored `type`, the `label` editors, run histories and drafters name it by, and for a step that acts on one of the plugin's records, `picks` — the site collection it lists them from (one the plugin declares under `hostCollections`), the step fields holding the pick, and the words for the picker and for a step with none. `offered: false` keeps a step only an automation holds out of the besigner's interaction builder; `holds` marks a step that suspends the run, with the band of whole minutes it may hold and the `timeoutField` a hold that ran out of time leaves in scope, and a visitor's page never runs a step past one; `typedFields` are the fields a person types words into, each with the words a sentence `names` it by, where a drafted step may leave a bracketed placeholder. Compiled into the catalog file and read by core `site-interactions.ts` and `draft-placeholders.ts`. `hostEvents` (AGL-3080) = the host events the plugin's server doors raise with `emitHostEvent`: the `type` an automation's trigger stores (never renamed), its `order` in every trigger picker (the platform's own `pageView` is 20), the `label` pickers and run rows show, and the `payloadKeys` it puts in scope; compiled into `app-utils/plugin-host-events.generated.ts` and read by core `host-events.ts`, because the event bus, the trigger pickers and the validators read them with no plugin loaded. `containers` (AGL-3080) = the container kinds the plugin keeps — a document other records are filed under by naming its id in `<kind>Ids` on their own document, a campaign being the first — with the org collection a picker reads them from; compiled into core `plugin-manager/plugin-containers.generated.ts`, which the membership helpers and the container picker read. `mobile` (AGL-3620) = the plugin's surface in the Aglyn mobile apps: `register` names the registrar its `./mobile` entry (`src/mobile/index.ts`, never re-exported from a web entry) exports, and `contributes` lists the ids it registers by kind (`screens`, `tabs`, `widgets`, `quickActions`, `deepLinks`); the generator compiles them into the SEPARATE `apps/mobile/src/plugins.mobile.generated.ts`, the only manifest a mobile app reads, so the web manifests never change for it, and the app's loader refuses a registration the declaration does not name. `subscriptionTopics` (AGL-3080) = the streams the plugin's mail is sent under, which a recipient can leave one at a time (`id` is a wire value: it rides in every signed unsubscribe link and keys every recorded opt-out, so it is never renamed), in the preference page's `order`; exactly one plugin marks its topic `default`, the stream a campaign or a scheduled automated email belongs to when it names none. Compiled into core `plugin-manager/plugin-subscription-topics.generated.ts`, the built-in floor of every org's topic catalog.

catalog.label: Components
catalog.description: The base component and theme library every site builds on.

catalog.$comment: On for every workspace and switchable per site (AGL-3029): the catalog and the submissions already stored belong to the workspace. A site's switch reaches every half of a form through this id, so no half keeps running behind a page that no longer shows it.
catalog.label: Forms
catalog.description: Forms on the site and the catalog that owns them.

siteOff.stops: Switching Forms off for this site stops forms rendering on its published pages, refuses every submission sent to it, and blocks publishing a form, or a page that carries one, until Forms is back on.
siteOff.keeps: Submissions already received, the workspace’s form catalog and the CRM leads its forms created are kept, and forms keep working on the workspace’s other sites.

pages.heading: These published pages carry a form. Their forms stop rendering and stop accepting submissions:
pages.none: No published page on this site carries a form.

siteExport.$comment: A form's definition and published design (AGL-3533), never its submissions. The design is the parent's `rootId`/`nodes`; `versionId` is left off because the bundle carries no version documents, and a dangling pointer stops the editor minting version 1 (the component rule). The list keys and `stats` are what a live form carries: a restore writes with merge:false, so a key left off is erased, and the Forms list queries `retired` and `inCampaign`. Created only through the platform's create route, which counts it against `formsPerHost`.

hostCollections.name: formSubmissions
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: Visitor form submissions. Unbounded, PII-heavy, and a file attached to one is the visitor's upload — not a library asset an author picked, and not something deleting a library asset would break.

hostEvents.$comment: `formId` is the submitted form's id, present only when the form exists on the site (AGL-3458), so a condition keyed on it survives the form being renamed where one on `formName` does not.
hostEvents.label: Form submitted
payloadKeys: and every submitted field by name

words.cause: This usually means a bot is filling in one of your forms — if it is real traffic, contact support and we will raise the limit.

transferResources.$comment: AGL-3532. Personal data: the export route needs “Manage data” on the site and audits every file. Opened on one form, the columns are that form’s questions (`ctx.filter.formId`). Export only: A submission is what a visitor sent through a published form, stamped with the time and the page it came from; a file cannot have sent one, so submissions are exported and never imported.
transferResources.label: Form submissions
transferResources.description: What visitors sent through this site’s forms: each answer, and when, on which page and through which form it arrived.

mobile.$comment: AGL-3652: today's bookings at the Aglyn POS counter, paid on the device's own card reader through bookings/in-person-payment.

catalog.label: Bookings
catalog.description: Services, open slots, and paid bookings.

resource.label: services
resource.$comment: `crmFollowUpTask` and `crmMeetingActivity` are the two CRM switches a service carries (AGL-2660): whether a booking files a meeting on the record, and whether it owes a follow-up task. `askPhone` and `askAddress` are what the booking widget asks the booker for beyond a name and an email (AGL-3493): off, optional or required. `priceDisplay` is how the price is stated (AGL-3475): fixed (absent), or a label (varies, estimate, contact) that books with no charge.

hostCollections.name: bookings
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: Booking records — a customer, a time and a service pointer. The service holds the imagery and IS scanned; a booking is the transaction against it.

transferResources.$comment: AGL-3532. Export only: the one write path that creates a booking (`bookings/book`) emails the customer and may charge them, and the reminder job would email any booking it found. Export only: A booking is made on the booking page, which holds the slot, takes any payment and sends the confirmation and the reminder; one written from a file would skip all of that, so bookings are exported and never imported. AGL-3548: the Bookings page's plan feature (`bookings`) gates both directions, as the page does.
transferResources.label: Bookings
transferResources.description: Every booking on this site: the service, the time, the customer’s details, its status and what was paid.

mobile.$comment: AGL-3621: the Aglyn app's store screens. Orders (list, detail, fulfill, refund, receipt print and share), products (list, edit, camera photos to the DAM, stock), barcode scan, and the sales and traffic dashboard; list and detail split side by side on tablets.

android.$comment: AGL-3652: the Aglyn POS register (item grid, basket, checkout, receipt), its card readers panel and today's bookings at the counter; the Aglyn app's store screens open the console's pages until their native versions land.

catalog.$comment: The Members blocks and the membership/* handlers are registered by this bundle, so there is no separate package to load; what this id contributes is the SWITCH the tenant route gate, the console card and the sitemap all ask (AGL-2486). Commerce off = member pages with no server, hence requires.
catalog.label: User Accounts
catalog.description: Visitor accounts on the site: the /signin, /signup and /recover pages, and the Members blocks. On for a new site; a site created before that stays off until you turn it on.

releaseFlagDefinition.label: User Accounts
releaseFlagDefinition.description: Visitor accounts on published sites: the /signin, /signup and /recover pages and the Members blocks (AGL-2486). Platform-wide kill switch only — whether a given SITE serves those pages is the per-site User Accounts toggle, which is off until a site opts in.

catalog.label: Commerce
catalog.description: Products, carts, checkout, orders, POS.

releaseFlagDefinition.label: Commerce v2
releaseFlagDefinition.description: Full ecommerce wave: catalog/variants, cart + checkout, digital goods, reservations, POS, and the repriced commerce tiers (AGL-276..331).

resource.label: products
resource.$comment: The whole product model: the editor, the duplicate action and the CSV importer each send a full product. `nameLower`, `nameTokens`, `nameReversed`, `skus`, `barcodes`, `priceFromCents`, `soldOut` and `collectionIds` are the search, price, stock and smart-collection keys this plugin derives on the payload (`productSearchFields`, `productStockFields`, `productCollectionIds`; AGL-2501, AGL-3321), so they are allow-listed rather than stamped. `priceUsd`, `inventory` and `imageUrl` are the legacy Commerce Starter fields every caller still writes. Born live — `deletedAt: null` — because the products table queries `deletedAt == null` and Firestore cannot match an absent field; a duplicate never carries its source's soft delete.

hostCollections.name: siteMemberCredentials
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: A site member's password hash, one document per member, read and written only by the membership routes (AGL-3308). A credential with no content field, and no client may read it.

hostCollections.name: orders
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: Completed orders. Line items COPY a product's `imageUrl` at purchase time, so these would match — and matching would be the wrong answer: an order is an immutable record of what was sold, deleting the asset changes nothing about it, and no author can edit one. A busy store also holds more of these than the whole read budget.

hostCollections.name: carts
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: Live and abandoned carts, with the same copied line-item image and the same reasoning, at higher volume — one document per shopper session.

hostCollections.name: checkouts
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: In-flight checkout sessions. Transient buyer state carrying the same line-item snapshot as `carts`.

hostCollections.name: reservations
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: POS and booking holds. Short-lived transaction rows pointing at a resource that is itself scanned.

hostCollections.name: stockHolds
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: Inventory holds taken during checkout. Machine-written, short-lived, and a quantity rather than content.

hostCollections.name: subscriptions
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: Site membership subscriptions: a plan pointer, a status and Stripe ids. Server-written from the billing webhook.

hostCollections.name: registers
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: POS register allocations — a count against the register add-on, read by billing (AGL-1775). No content field at all.

resource.label: POS registers
resource.$comment: The count is met against the site's allocation of the org's register seats (AGL-1775), which the platform resolves from this quota key; `pos` gates POS at all.

hostCollections.name: giftCards
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: Gift card balances and redemption history. Money, not content.

hostCollections.name: licenseKeys
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: Digital-product license keys issued at fulfilment: a code, an order pointer and a revocation flag.

hostCollections.name: inventoryAdjustments
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: The append-only stock adjustment ledger (AGL-2269). One row per manual stock edit and per cancellation release, unbounded over a store's life.

hostCollections.name: inventoryReconciliation
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: Reconciliation runs comparing counted stock against recorded stock. Machine-written totals.

hostCollections.name: restockAlerts
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: Back-in-stock requests: an email address and a product pointer, written by visitors.

hostCollections.name: stripeTaxRates
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: Cached Stripe tax rate ids, written by the tax sync. Vendor ids.

hostCollections.name: returns
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: Returns (AGL-3611): line indexes, quantities, reasons and a return label link, written only by the returns routes. A return names no image of its own; the order's lines carry the copies, and the order is not scanned for the same reason.

hostCollections.name: orderWebhooks
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: The merchant's outbound order webhook endpoints (AGL-3611): a URL and the event names it takes. Scanning reads every endpoint for a URL that is never a media file.

hostCollections.name: orderWebhookSecrets
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: Sealed HMAC signing secrets for the order webhooks (AGL-3611). Reading them for media would put a secret on a scan path to match nothing.

hostCollections.name: orderWebhookDeliveries
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: The webhook delivery log (AGL-3611): one row per event per endpoint, expiring after 30 days. A body copies the order, whose image URLs record what was sold rather than use the file, so a match would be wrong, and a busy store holds thousands.

hostCollections.name: posStaffPins
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: Register staff PINs (AGL-3609): a salted hash and a lockout counter per member, written only by the staff PIN route. No content field at all.

hostCollections.name: terminal
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: The site's Stripe Terminal Location (AGL-3607): a vendor id and the address it was registered with, written only by the reader routes. No content field.

hostCollections.name: terminalReaders
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: The site's card readers (AGL-3607): a Stripe reader id, a label and a status, written only by `/api/commerce/pos-readers`. No content field.

hostCollections.name: printers
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: Cloud receipt printers (AGL-3619): a device id, a secret version, a paper width and a status. A receipt logo is the one stored IN the printer and named by a key code, never a file URL, so nothing here can use an asset.

hostCollections.name: printJobs
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: The printers' queue (AGL-3619): rendered receipt, ticket and label bytes waiting for a printer's poll, written by the print routes and gone once printed. Printer commands, not content, and a busy register queues hundreds a day.

sitemapSections.$comment: A product page for each active product with a slug, once the store names the template products render through (AGL-299). Soft deletes keep `status: active`, hence skipWhen. Commerce stamps epoch milliseconds.
The catalog collections served at /collections/{slug} (AGL-954), once the store names their template. A content collection is the platform's own section.

hostEvents.$comment: Order and return events (AGL-3611): raised through the plugin event outbox and handed to the host event bus by commerce's own subscriber, so they reach an automation at least once and within a minute of the fact.
hostEvents.label: Order paid

subscriptionTopics.name: Newsletter
subscriptionTopics.description: Regular news and stories from us.

subscriptionTopics.name: Product updates
subscriptionTopics.description: New products, restocks and changes to what we offer.

transferResources.$comment: Products and their variants, a row per variant (AGL-3531): matched by handle, then SKU, then ID, and updated on a match; Shopify's product CSV maps column for column, and the Shopify preset writes one.
transferResources.label: Products
transferResources.description: Products with their options, variants, prices, stock, images and search listing.

transferResources.label: Product categories
transferResources.description: The category tree products are filed under, matched by slug, then name.

transferResources.$comment: Exported only: an order is the record of a sale. The upload refuses a file, the hub offers no Import, and every row is still refused at the dry run.
transferResources.label: Orders
transferResources.description: Every order with its items, money, customer and addresses. Exported only.

transferResources.label: Discounts
transferResources.description: Discount codes and automatic promotions, matched by code, then name. New ones start switched off.

transferResources.label: Coupons
transferResources.description: Percent-off coupon codes, matched by code. New ones start switched off.

transferResources.$comment: Imported by ISSUING each card through the plugin's issue path (AGL-3551), never by writing a balance: owners and admins only, the dry run lists every card and asks for the total typed back, and undo voids only cards nobody has spent from. A card's ID is its code. AGL-3548: issuing cards needs the plan's gift cards (`giftCards`), as the Gift cards card's issue route does; the cards a workspace already holds stay readable, and exportable, on every plan. AGL-3554: imported by the workspace’s owners and admins and the site’s admins alone (importRoles), as an import issues spendable money.
transferResources.label: Gift cards
transferResources.description: Every gift card's code, balance and status. An import issues each card, confirmed by the total.

transferResources.$comment: A file of tracking numbers ships the orders it names (AGL-3613): each row is a parcel matched to its order by number, recorded through the order’s own shipment path (the buyer is emailed), once per tracking number. A row for an order with nothing left to ship replaces its tracking only when the person chooses Overwrite. Nothing creates an order. Export lists every shipment with its tracking.
transferResources.label: Tracking numbers
transferResources.description: Tracking numbers from a label tool, each recorded as a shipment on the order it names.

consoleRedirects.$comment: The address the marketplace had under Manage before it became an organization section (AGL-236). A checkout with no site to return to still lands here, so it keeps resolving.

catalog.label: Marketplace
catalog.description: Marketplace listings, templates, and installs.

releaseFlagDefinition.$comment: navTabId (AGL-1654) is the marketplace plugin's own `orgNavItems` entry, held to a real declaration by `release-flag-nav-tab-ids.spec.ts`; the page behind it is gated (AGL-2019), so off means off.
releaseFlagDefinition.label: Marketplace
releaseFlagDefinition.description: Marketplace browsing, publishing and plugin installs.

notificationCategories.$comment: The id is persisted: every person's preferences for listing reviews are stored under `marketplace`, so it keeps this spelling.
notificationCategories.label: Marketplace
notificationCategories.description: Decisions on plugin listings you submitted for review.

consoleRedirects.$comment: The organization's address book, before it became the contacts section of the organization-level CRM (AGL-2630). Permanent, so a link kept from before — a bookmark, a docs page, an email — is corrected by the browser rather than followed twice; a reader the hub refuses is refused there, with the reason.

catalog.$comment: The id was contacts until AGL-2595 widened one list into the hub; the release flag kept its key because it is persisted in Remote Config.
catalog.label: CRM
catalog.description: Leads, contacts, companies, deals, tasks and reports.

releaseFlagDefinition.label: CRM
releaseFlagDefinition.description: The CRM: contacts, leads, companies, deals, tasks, reports and fields.

hostCollections.name: leads
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: Captured leads, on the same footing as `formSubmissions`: visitor-submitted, unbounded, and never a place an author places an asset.

notificationDigests.$comment: The key is persisted in every person's `digestPrefs`; the daily digest route reads the same one.
notificationDigests.label: Daily CRM digest
notificationDigests.description: Each morning: your overdue and due-today tasks and the leads nobody has worked, here and by email.

hostEvents.$comment: Raised when a capture files a NEW lead — a lead-routed form or a booking request (AGL-3232). `formId` is present only when a form filed it (AGL-3458), and `campaignIds` only when the capture surface is filed under campaigns, comma-joined as on `contactCreated`.
hostEvents.label: New lead

hostEvents.$comment: Raised by the console's `crm/task-complete` route rather than by a Firestore trigger, so the payload names who completed the task and what it hung off (AGL-2599).
hostEvents.label: CRM task completed

hostEvents.$comment: `formId` is present only when the capture came through a form (AGL-2626), so `formId` equals a form's id is the condition that picks that form's people out of every other door's.
hostEvents.label: Contact created

transferResources.$comment: AGL-3527. Workspace records; opened under a site, a transfer reads that site's view and an import files new people under it. AGL-3555: like every CRM resource it moves only on a plan with the CRM (featureFlag), except that the contacts and leads EXPORTS stay on every plan, the people files of Settings → Privacy.
transferResources.label: Contacts
transferResources.description: Every contact field, custom fields included, with the company, the manager and the owner by name.

transferResources.label: Companies
transferResources.description: Every company field, custom fields included, with the parent company and the owner by name.

transferResources.label: Email templates
transferResources.description: Shared email templates and snippets, and your own personal ones.

transferResources.label: Leads
transferResources.description: Every lead field, custom fields included, with the status, the owner and the campaigns by name.

transferResources.$comment: AGL-3528. Matched by Aglyn ID or the external id another CRM gave the deal, so a file imported twice updates rather than duplicates.
transferResources.label: Deals
transferResources.description: Every deal field, custom fields and contact roles included, with the pipeline, stage, contact and company by name.

transferResources.label: Tasks
transferResources.description: Every task, with its type, priority and status as your lists label them and the contact, company and deal it is for.

transferResources.label: Activities
transferResources.description: Every call, email, meeting and note the team logged, with who logged it and what it was about.

transferResources.label: Pipelines and stages
transferResources.description: Each pipeline with its stages in order: their kind, probability and forecast category.

transferResources.label: Custom fields
transferResources.description: Every custom field you defined, on which record, of what type, with its choices.

transferResources.$comment: AGL-3548: Sequences' entitlement (`outreach`) gates both directions, as every Sequences route does.
transferResources.label: Sequences
transferResources.description: Each sequence's steps and settings, imported as a draft. Never who was enrolled or what was sent.

transferResources.$comment: AGL-3532. Add-only: a row never changes or removes an entry, because the list is a promise not to email someone. AGL-3548: Sequences' entitlement (`outreach`) gates both directions, as every Sequences route does.
transferResources.label: Do-not-contact list
transferResources.description: The domains and addresses sequences never email. An import only adds to it; an address is kept as a fingerprint, so only domains are exported.

catalog.$comment: Works the CRM's records but is released and entitled on its own (AGL-2974). Reads Sequences since AGL-3199; the id is stored on every org, so it stays.
catalog.label: Sequences
catalog.description: One-to-one email sequences sent from connected mailboxes.

releaseFlagDefinition.$comment: The plugin's kill switch as well as its launch gate (AGL-2974). OFF by default, because nothing behind it sent mail at launch and no plan carries the `outreach` entitlement it also needs. The KEY stays `release_outreach`: it is persisted in Remote Config (AGL-3199).
releaseFlagDefinition.label: Sequences
releaseFlagDefinition.description: One-to-one, multi-step email sequences sent from a rep’s own connected mailbox and logged in the CRM (AGL-2974). OFF by default and staff preview only. An organization also needs the `outreach` entitlement, which no plan carries, so a customer reaches it only through a per-org entitlement override.

subscriptionTopics.name: Sales outreach
subscriptionTopics.description: Messages from a person here about working together.

catalog.$comment: AGL-3614. Posts commerce sales, refunds, fees and payouts to QuickBooks Online or Xero. Sold with commerce: the extension's entitlement is `features.commerce`, so no plan and no add-on of its own.
catalog.label: Accounting
catalog.description: Sales, refunds, fees and payouts posted to QuickBooks Online or Xero.

releaseFlagDefinition.$comment: OFF by default and the release gate for an env-gated feature: switch it on only for a deployment whose console has an Intuit or Xero app's credentials and the accounting token key (the variables are named in libs/plugins/accounting/README.md). The docs guard holds the Connect QuickBooks Online and Connect Xero guides unclaimed while it is off.
releaseFlagDefinition.label: Accounting
releaseFlagDefinition.description: QuickBooks Online and Xero sync for commerce: sales receipts or a daily summary journal, refunds, platform fees and Stripe payouts, with a mapping page and a sync log (AGL-3614). OFF by default; needs the deployment's Intuit or Xero app credentials and the accounting token key on the console.

hostCollections.name: recordPages
hostCollections.label: record template
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: A binding holds a dataset id, a base path and field ids — never a value. The images a record page shows are the record's own, in the organization's dataset records, which no site collection holds.

sitemapReaders.$comment: Record pages (AGL-3475): one child sitemap per record template on a site, records-{base}, listing every record with a page address. The reader registers from serverDeclarations.

siteBundleSections.$comment: A site's datasets and their records, which live under the organization and are narrowed to the site on the way out; a restore validates each record against its dataset's model and meets the count against the datasets the workspace has paid for, add-ons included.

artifactTypes.$comment: A dataset's schema, published from a dataset and installed as a new, empty one; the installer asks this plugin to read, write and update the copy, and never reads the datasets collection itself.

catalog.label: Data
catalog.description: Datasets, records, and CSV import/export.

releaseFlagDefinition.label: Data store
releaseFlagDefinition.description: Datasets, models and dynamic data bindings.

transferResources.$comment: A dataset's records (AGL-3530), one dataset at a time: reached as data.dataset:<datasetId>, so a job, a person's remembered export fields and the one running import each belong to one dataset. The server half registers from consoleServerDeclarations, the client half from the console registrar. readableByMembers (AGL-3546): every member may read a dataset they can see, so every such member may export it; the resource checks the dataset's visibility itself. AGL-3548: the Data page's plan feature (`dataStore`) gates both directions, as the page and the datasets API do.
transferResources.label: Dataset records
transferResources.description: The records of one dataset, with every field it defines.

consoleRedirects.$comment: The hub's first section is named for the record it lists (`Emails / Messages`), not for the surface holding it. `:path*` matches zero segments as well as many, so the bare section and every message's own page arrive. A redirect rather than a section alias: a second id answering to the same body would give one page two addresses, which is what a canonical URL is for.

The organization's messages left its Marketing hub for its own Emails page, where a site's have always been (AGL-3300). `:path*` carries the bare list, one message and its `/edit` across, and cannot reach a site's hub: `/:orgSlug/hosts/:host/marketing/…` has `hosts` where this has `marketing`.

transferResources.$comment: One list's members (AGL-3529): imported INTO a list and exported FROM one, one list at a time as email.list-members:<listId>, opened from the list's page. Every address goes through the gate a typed one does; the statement of permission is the plugin's own wizard step; 50,000 rows a file is LIST_IMPORT_MAX_ADDRESSES (list-import.ts).
transferResources.label: List members
transferResources.description: The people on one email list, with the consent each was added under.

transferResources.$comment: A site's suppression list (AGL-3529). An import only adds: an address already suppressed is left as it is, and nothing removes one.
transferResources.label: Suppressions
transferResources.description: The addresses a site's marketing email skips, and why.

transferResources.$comment: The organization's email topics as workspace package items (AGL-3550): a topic's name, description, retired flag and confirmation setting, written through the topic page's own document shape. Never an opt-out or a confirmation — those are a person's, per site.
transferResources.label: Email topics
transferResources.description: Each topic's name, what recipients are told they get, and whether it is retired. Never who chose it.

catalog.label: Email
catalog.description: Designed emails and campaign sending.

releaseFlagDefinition.label: Email
releaseFlagDefinition.description: Designed emails, campaigns, and audience sending.

hostCollections.name: suppressions
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: Unsubscribes, bounces and spam complaints. Email addresses and a reason.

catalog.label: Events Calendar
catalog.description: Event lists and calendars.

siteExport.$comment: A site's calendar events (AGL-3533). No attendee or RSVP data exists on them. A deleted event carries `deletedAt` and is left out by the export.

count.uncapped: The events page creates an event with a client write and no count, so a restore mints nothing an editor could not already.

transferResources.$comment: AGL-3532. AGL-3548: the Event Calendar add-on (`eventCalendar`) gates both directions, as the Events page does.
transferResources.label: Events
transferResources.description: This site’s calendar events, matched on their ID, then the title and start together.

catalog.label: Inbox
catalog.description: Form submissions and lead inbox.

releaseFlagDefinition.label: Inbox
releaseFlagDefinition.description: Form submissions, site members, and the lead inbox.

catalog.label: Logic
catalog.description: Variables, functions, and reference health.

releaseFlagDefinition.label: Logic
releaseFlagDefinition.description: Variables, no-code functions, and reference health.

transferResources.label: Campaigns
transferResources.description: Each campaign's name, dates, lists and its emails' copy, imported as drafts. Never what was sent or its results.

catalog.label: Marketing
catalog.description: Overlays, campaigns, and experiments.

releaseFlagDefinition.label: Marketing
releaseFlagDefinition.description: Overlays, campaigns at-a-glance, and A/B experiments.

siteExport.$comment: A/B experiments (AGL-3533): the design and the outcome. The per-variant counters live in the `stats` subcollection and do not travel. A variant's `versionId` names a version of the experiment's page, and a package carries only a page's published version, so on another site the variants are picked again.

count.uncapped: The experiments card creates an experiment with a client write and no count, so a restore mints nothing an editor could not already.

siteExport.$comment: Announcement bars and popups (AGL-3533). `stats` is carried because the editor writes the whole document back with it, so a live overlay always holds one.

count.uncapped: The overlays card creates a bar or popup with a client write and no count, so a restore mints nothing an editor could not already.

hostCollections.name: campaignAttributions
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: One row per conversion — a form submission, a lead, a contact or a booking — recording which campaign the visitor arrived from. Written only by the Admin SDK, and the whole record is three sanitized UTM strings capped at a hundred characters: there is no field an asset could occupy and no surface that could pick one into it. Unbounded on the same footing as the conversions it credits.

orgCollections.name: emailCampaigns
orgCollections.mediaScanReason: The campaign CONTAINER — a name, a date window, the list ids it is aimed at, a topic and the sites it runs on. Distinct from `campaigns`, which holds the sends and IS scanned because a send carries the copy that went out. A container carries no copy and no asset reference: the design a send renders is a screen, and the screen is where the picker writes.

mobile.$comment: AGL-3620: the sample mobile registration. The site's rules as a native list (a split view on tablets), a dashboard count, a quick action, and the console's Redirects page opening natively from a link or a notification.

catalog.label: Redirects
catalog.description: URL redirect rules.

resource.label: redirects
resource.$comment: A routing statement over the whole live site the moment it exists, not a draft (AGL-1881, AGL-2573): it needs the publishing role, an off-platform destination carries the uid of the publisher who chose it (the serve path refuses one without), and its source is announced to the site cache on create.

siteExport.$comment: A site's redirects (AGL-3533). `externalDestinationApprovedBy` is never read from a file: a restore stamps the admin who imported it on a destination off the site. `lastHitAt` is when it last fired here and does not travel.

transferResources.$comment: AGL-3532. Written through the same allow-list, quota, publish role and approval stamp the redirects page and the create route use; the approver of an off-site destination is the person importing, never a column of the file. AGL-3548: the Redirects page's plan feature (`redirects`) gates both directions, as the page does; rules without it are not served either.
transferResources.label: Redirects
transferResources.description: This site’s redirect rules, matched on the path they redirect from.

transferResources.$comment: AGL-3548: org automations' plan feature (`actions`) gates both directions, as their section and their create route do.
transferResources.label: Org automations
transferResources.description: The organization's automations — trigger, steps and sites — imported switched off.

consoleRedirects.$comment: Workflows became Automation: the section holds a Workflows tab, so the parent could not keep the name. Next carries the query string across, so the tab deep links (`?tab=actions`, `?tab=webhooks`) survive; their ids never changed. `automation-section.spec.ts` holds the retired address.

catalog.$comment: The id is stored on every org's enabled-plugin list; only the label moved.
catalog.label: Automation
catalog.description: Workflows, actions, webhooks, and run logs.

releaseFlagDefinition.label: Automation
releaseFlagDefinition.description: Workflows, actions, webhooks and their run history.

duplicate.$comment: The trigger is cleared, so a copy runs nothing until somebody arms it.

siteExport.$comment: `trigger` is written as a literal null by the edit path, so absence and null are different states and a restore keeps the null.

resource.label: webhooks
resource.$comment: Capped from a server read, never a client count (AGL-1360). `secret` stays client-supplied: it is generated with crypto.getRandomValues and the site's own editors read it off the card anyway.

resource.label: interactions and actions
resource.$comment: No entitlement (AGL-2266): the paid actions flag and the free interactions both write this collection, so the flag decides what RUNS, not what may be created. The full action model, because the actions card, the interaction builder and the preset wiring each send it.

siteExport.$comment: The stored shape `hostActionDocument` writes, which is narrower than the create's list: every creator now creates a shell and merge-sets the rest. `recipe` is the stamp of the recipe an action began as (AGL-2639).

orgCollections.name: automations
orgCollections.mediaScanReason: An org automation (AGL-3302) — a trigger, its conditions, the sites it is placed on, and a step list drawn from the server steps only: email subject and body as plain text, list, dataset and campaign ids, CRM fields and waits. No step it may hold carries a media reference, the in-page steps that could (custom HTML, popups) are refused by its save route, and it is written only by that route.

catalog.$comment: On for every workspace, off for a site only when that site says so, and no release flag (AGL-2939): the workspace half (the add-on, credits, allotments, overage billing, the staff doors) carries no site and must keep running whatever any one site decides. Its doors gate themselves one by one; a flag on the bundle would switch off the released doors with the unreleased ones.
catalog.label: AI
catalog.description: The assistant, generative building and automation, and the AI add-on.

siteOff.stops: Switching AI off for this site hides the assistant, Create with AI, the AI cards and the editor’s AI controls on this site, refuses every AI request made for it, and stops its queued AI jobs without spending credits.
siteOff.keeps: It does not stop the workspace’s AI add-on, credits, allotments or overage billing, and AI keeps working on the workspace’s other sites.

orgCollections.name: aiJobs
orgCollections.label: AI job
orgCollections.mediaScanReason: An AI job is the machine's record of one request: the brief, scalar inputs, the step ledger and the ids of the documents it produced. What it produced is a screen, layout, product or other document of the site, and the scan reads that document; scanning the job would report a request as using an asset the page it built uses. Jobs expire on their own (`expiresAt`, 180 days).

plugins.$comment: AGL-3656: the platform's fonts. serverDeclarations registers the Google Fonts catalog (families, weights, italics and the metrics of each regular face) as core's theme font catalog, which a published page loads its theme fonts by: only the faces a family offers, and a local fallback sized to the family's metrics. console fills the theme editor's Typography card (`themeEditorFonts`) with the font picker (the whole Google Fonts catalog, previews in the site's own words, pairings, cost) and the font installer, which uploads a site's own font files. consoleApi serves /api/fonts/cost, what a theme's fonts cost a visitor worked out as the published page loads them, and /api/fonts/prepare, which checks an uploaded file's embedding license and converts and subsets it to WOFF2 with harfbuzz; the file is then stored through the media library's own upload and replace routes. Always on: a published page's fonts are part of its theme, so there is no switch to turn them off.

catalog.label: Fonts
catalog.description: Upload your own fonts and pick from the Google Fonts catalog for your site's theme.

catalog.$comment: On for every workspace, off for a site only when that site says so (AGL-3405): the built-in themes cost nothing until the theme page lists them, and a site that picked one keeps it whatever this switch says, because picking a theme copies it onto the site.
catalog.label: Themes
catalog.description: Built-in themes to pick from on Setup → Theme: Bootstrap, Minimal and Material 3.

siteOff.stops: Switching Themes off for this site removes its built-in themes from the theme picker.
siteOff.keeps: A site already using one keeps it, with every edit made to it: picking a theme copies it onto the site, so nothing on the published site changes.

plugins.$comment: AGL-3610: text messages behind core's core.messaging.sms contract (Twilio adapter). Infrastructure, like video-delivery: no catalog entry and no switch. Inert until TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID, TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN and TWILIO_MESSAGING_SERVICE_SID are set. consoleApi serves Twilio's signed inbound STOP webhook at /api/sms/inbound.

orgKeyedCollections.$comment: A tracking number's workspace, site and record, so a provider's webhook finds what it is about (AGL-3612). Top level, so org erasure removes them by orgId.
orgKeyedCollections.name: shippingTrackers

orgKeyedCollections.$comment: Carrier quotes kept ten minutes, and the quote a label is bought from (AGL-3612).
orgKeyedCollections.name: shippingQuoteCache

catalog.$comment: Carrier rates at checkout, labels, tracking and address checks for the commerce plugin's orders (AGL-3612), through core's shipping-rate and shipment-record seams; it never imports commerce. No `requires` edge: a workspace cannot switch it off, so an edge to commerce would refuse every set that switches commerce off; instead it runs only on a site where commerce is on (site-context.ts). On for every workspace like AI, off for a site only when that site says so, and no release flag: every surface hides itself until the deployment names a provider (SHIPPO_API_TOKEN or EASYPOST_API_KEY, with SHIPPING_TOKEN_KEY), or offers a merchant's own Easyship, Sendcloud or ShipperHQ account (SHIPPING_OWN_ACCOUNT_PROVIDERS with SHIPPING_TOKEN_KEY, AGL-3632).
catalog.label: Shipping
catalog.description: Carrier rates at checkout, shipping labels and tracking for physical orders, where the platform has connected a carrier provider.

siteOff.stops: Switching Shipping off for this site stops live carrier rates at its checkout, which falls back to the site’s own shipping rates, and removes label buying from its orders.
siteOff.keeps: Labels already bought, their tracking and their charges are kept, and Shipping keeps working on the workspace’s other sites.

catalog.$comment: AfterShip tracking, Route package protection and Narvar for the commerce plugin's orders (AGL-3635), each with the merchant's own account, through core's checkout-extras and tracking-pages seams and commerce's order events by name; it never imports commerce. No `requires` edge, for shipping's reason: a workspace cannot switch it off, so it runs only on a site where commerce is on (site-context.ts). On for every workspace, off for a site only when that site says so, and no release flag: every surface hides itself until the deployment sets POST_PURCHASE_VENDORS and POST_PURCHASE_TOKEN_KEY.
catalog.label: Tracking and protection
catalog.description: Parcel tracking through AfterShip, package protection at checkout through Route, and Narvar order tracking, with the store's own accounts.

siteOff.stops: Switching Tracking and protection off for this site stops offering package protection in its cart, following new parcels and sending new orders to Narvar.
siteOff.keeps: Protection already bought stays open with Route, connected accounts stay connected, and it keeps working on the workspace's other sites.

orgKeyedCollections.$comment: A site's connection to its own Avalara or TaxJar account, the credential sealed (AGL-3631). Top level and closed to every client, so org erasure removes them by orgId.
orgKeyedCollections.name: taxEngineConnections

orgKeyedCollections.$comment: One product's tax code at the connected tax service (AGL-3631).
orgKeyedCollections.name: taxEngineProductCodes

orgKeyedCollections.$comment: A customer the merchant recorded as tax-exempt, by email (AGL-3631).
orgKeyedCollections.name: taxEngineExemptions

orgKeyedCollections.$comment: One order as recorded with the tax service, and the refunds reversed against it (AGL-3631).
orgKeyedCollections.name: taxEngineTransactions

catalog.$comment: Outside sales tax engines (AGL-3631): a merchant connects their OWN Avalara AvaTax or TaxJar account, and commerce asks it for tax through core's core.tax-engine contract; paid orders and refunds are recorded there through commerce's order events. It never imports commerce. No `requires` edge, for the reason shipping gives: a workspace cannot switch it off, so an edge to commerce would refuse every set that switches commerce off; instead it runs only on a site where commerce is on (site-context.ts). On for every workspace, off for a site only when that site says so, and no release flag: every surface hides itself until the deployment sets TAX_ENGINES_TOKEN_KEY, the key merchants' credentials are sealed under. Aglyn holds no vendor account.
catalog.label: Tax services
catalog.description: Sales tax from your own Avalara AvaTax or TaxJar account at checkout and the register.

siteOff.stops: Switching Tax services off for this site stops checkout and the register asking its connected tax service, which then use the site’s own tax rates, and stops recording its paid orders there.
siteOff.keeps: The connection, product tax codes and exempt customers are kept, and orders already recorded stay recorded.

orgKeyedCollections.$comment: A site's connection to the merchant's OWN Mailchimp, Klaviyo, Omnisend or Attentive account, the credential sealed, with its sync cursors and its log subcollection (AGL-3639). Top level and closed to every client, so org erasure removes them by orgId.
orgKeyedCollections.name: marketingPlatformConnections

orgKeyedCollections.$comment: Commerce events owed to one connection, written by the event subscriber and delivered by the console job (AGL-3639).
orgKeyedCollections.name: marketingPlatformEvents

catalog.$comment: Two-way contact and consent sync with a merchant's OWN email platform (AGL-3639): Mailchimp, Klaviyo and Omnisend by the merchant's own API key, and by OAuth where the deployment registered the app (MAILCHIMP_CLIENT_ID/SECRET, KLAVIYO_CLIENT_ID/SECRET); Attentive only with its partner app (ATTENTIVE_CLIENT_ID/SECRET). It reaches the CRM's people only through core's person-records seam and each site's consent only through core's site-marketing-sync module, and commerce's events only through the domain-event outbox; it imports neither plugin. Sold with the CRM (`features.crm`), no price of its own. On for every workspace, off for a site only when that site says so, and no release flag: the card draws nothing until the console sets MARKETING_PLATFORMS_TOKEN_KEY, the key merchants' credentials are sealed under.
catalog.label: Email platforms
catalog.description: Two-way contact and unsubscribe sync with your own Mailchimp, Klaviyo or Omnisend account, and order events for their flows.

siteOff.stops: Switching Email platforms off for this site stops its contacts, unsubscribes and order events syncing with the email platforms it connected.
siteOff.keeps: The connections and everything already synced are kept, and an unsubscribe already read back stays on the site’s list.

hostCollections.name: salesChannels
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: A site's shopping-channel state (AGL-3637): one feed document per channel holding the token that locks its URL, the store's defaults for blank product fields, and a sealed OAuth token per API connection. No client reads or writes it, and nothing in it names a library asset.

catalog.$comment: AGL-3637. Product feeds of the commerce catalog for Google (and YouTube), Meta, TikTok, Pinterest, Snapchat and Microsoft, read through core's core.product-catalog contract; it never imports commerce. Like Shipping: on for every workspace, off for a site only when that site says so, no release flag, and it runs only on a site where commerce is on (server/site-gate.ts). Sold with commerce: its entitlement is `features.commerce`. The pre-channels Google address (/api/commerce/feed) is still commerce's route and answers through core.catalog-feed, registered from serverDeclarations. The Google Merchant API and Meta Catalog API connections are hidden until their env vars are set (libs/plugins/sales-channels/README.md).
catalog.label: Sales channels
catalog.description: Product feeds for Google, YouTube, Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, Pinterest, Snapchat and Microsoft Shopping.

siteOff.stops: Switching Sales channels off for this site stops every product feed it publishes, including the Google Merchant Center address set up before sales channels existed, so channels stop receiving updates.
siteOff.keeps: Each feed's address, its switch and the store's defaults are kept, so switching it back on resumes the same feeds.

catalog.$comment: On for every workspace, off for a site only when that site says so (AGL-3605): funnels are a way of reading the paid analytics tier, so the card needs no switch of its own to be sold, and it records nothing until a site saves its first funnel.
catalog.label: Funnels
catalog.description: Step-by-step conversion on a site's Analytics page: visits at each step, drop-off and time between steps.

siteOff.stops: Switching Funnels off for this site removes the Funnels card from its Analytics page.
siteOff.keeps: Saved funnels are kept, and visits keep being recorded while the site has one; delete the funnels to stop recording.

hostEvents.$comment: Raised by the funnels plugin's drop-off sweep (AGL-3605) once per person, funnel step and wait: a person who identified themselves by submitting a form reached `step` and had not reached the next step `afterHours` later, in this visit or any other of theirs. Never for an anonymous visit. Not the person's own action, so an email on it is a mailing with its unsubscribe link.
hostEvents.label: Left a funnel

hostCollections.name: funnels
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: A funnel is a name and its steps — paths and record ids, never an asset. Written only by the funnels save route.

hostCollections.name: funnelJourneys
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: One document per recorded visit: step types, paths or record ids, server times and UTM labels. Written only by the site collector on the Admin SDK, read only by the results route; expires 90 days after the visit.

hostCollections.name: funnelResults
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: A computed funnel result — counts, shares and durations — kept up to a day by the results route and expiring on its own.
